rows.title: Trump taps White House economist Stephen Miran to fill Fed vacancy on temporary basis
rows.standfirst: President Trump plans to nominate Stephen Miran to fill a vacant seat on the Federal Reserve's board of governors, but only for the next six months.

rows.title: 11 ways NPR readers resist the impulse to shop (plus, a poem for inspo)
rows.standfirst: Buying something new can be thrilling in the moment, but will you still be glad you bought it after the fact? NPR readers share their top tips for mindful shopping to avoid regret and overspending.

rows.title: Trump doubles tariffs on India, jeopardizing long-standing ties
rows.standfirst: Tensions are escalating between the U.S. and India as the Trump administration imposes tariffs and tries to force India to stop buying Russian oil.

rows.title: The legal case for — and against — Trump's tariffs
rows.standfirst: President Trump's new round of tariffs took effect today. It will bring in billions of dollars to the government, in part paid for by U.S. importers who can decide whether to pass that cost onto American families. But are these tariffs legal?

rows.title: Trump's broad tariffs go into effect, just as economic pain is surfacing
rows.standfirst: The White House said that starting just after midnight that goods from more than 60 countries and the European Union would face tariff rates of 10% or higher.

rows.title: United Airlines flights grounded nationwide because of computer problems
rows.standfirst: Hundreds of United Airlines flights were disrupted on Wednesday evening as the carrier grappled with a major computer system outage. The airline requested ground stops at its major hubs in the U.S.

rows.title: Claire's, the ear-piercing tween mall staple, is bankrupt — again
rows.standfirst: The chain's bankruptcy filing is the second in seven years. Its troubles include unwieldy debt, shoppers' changing habits and new tariff costs.

rows.title: Voice of America director says Trump officials are illegally ousting him
rows.standfirst: A judge is demanding answers about the international broadcaster's future from Trump official Kari Lake.

rows.title: What you need to know about the jobs report revisions
rows.standfirst: Why do revisions to the jobs report happen? Today on the show, we speak with a former Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics about why revisions occur and how we should interpret the monthly report's actual message.

rows.title: Summer School 5: The many ways governments influence industry
rows.standfirst: LIVE SHOW: August 18th in Brooklyn. Tickets here.

rows.title: Govt 5: The many ways governments influence industry (Industrial Policy)
rows.standfirst: LIVE SHOW: August 18th in Brooklyn. Tickets here.

rows.title: NFL and ESPN reach nonbinding agreement for sale of NFL Network and other media assets
rows.standfirst: Under the terms, ESPN will acquire NFL Network, NFL Fantasy and the rights to distribute the RedZone channel to cable and satellite operators and the league will get a 10% equity stake in ESPN.

rows.title: Drones delivering coffee? Trump administration wants more companies using UAVs
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration wants to make it easier for companies to use drones for business — from delivering coffee to inspecting power lines to working on farms.

rows.title: How you're using AI at work right now
rows.standfirst: Software engineers, teachers, a wedding photographer and more on how AI is changing their jobs.

rows.title: Can we still trust the monthly jobs report? (Update)
rows.standfirst: Since his return to office, President Trump has waged something of a pressure campaign on economic data and the people in charge of delivering it. His firing of the Bureau of Labor Statistics commissioner following a weak jobs report now has some wondering: can we still trust the official numbers? Today on the show, we're resharing our conversation with former BLS commissioner, Erica Groshen on her current fears for the integrity of government data. The original version of this story aired March 7, 2025.

rows.title: Anti-Trump podcast MeidasTouch is rivaling Joe Rogan. Does it have staying power?
rows.standfirst: The left-leaning media outfit has surged in Donald Trump's second term, appealing to progressives outraged by the president. Still, the online streaming world remains dominated by right-wing voices.

rows.title: Trump is tightening the screws on corporate America — and CEOs are staying mum
rows.standfirst: Critics warn that Trump's demands for business leaders to step down, and for the government to take a cut of sales, threaten American-style capitalism.

rows.title: Why every A-lister also has a side hustle
rows.standfirst: Seemingly every celebrity has their own brand these days, whether it’s booze (Cameron Diaz, Matthew McConaughey) or cosmetics (Selena Gomez, Lady Gaga) or squeezy food pouches (Jennifer Garner). Today on the show, what is fueling the celebrity business bonanza? We hear from two legendary singers, Lisa Loeb AND John Legend, who are pursuing ventures outside of show business.

rows.title: Why Trump's spending bill could close your grocery store
rows.standfirst: Trump’s tax and spending law makes the largest cut in history to one of the nation’s biggest safety net programs. Today on the show, we explore how cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, also known as SNAP, impacts families and grocery stores alike.

rows.title: Is Kari Lake a CEO? Her agency said so. The law suggests not
rows.standfirst: Kari Lake has sought to dismantle Voice of America and its federal parent, the U.S. Agency for Global Media. The agency has recently called her its acting CEO. But the law suggests she's not eligible for the job.

rows.title: Govt 6: When the markets need fixing (Market Design)
rows.standfirst: In economics, a market is a place (even virtual) where buyers and sellers interact to exchange goods or services. Economists love markets. It's like all of our supply and demand graphs have come to life. Everything you buy goes through some sort of marketplace—your cup of coffee came from trading in the bean markets. Your spouse might have come from the dating marketplace on the apps. Even kids will tell you one Snickers is worth at least two Twix.

rows.title: The hidden costs of cutting Medicaid
rows.standfirst: Cutting Medicaid can seem like an easy way to slash the budget. But, the costs can spread to all of us.

rows.title: Inflation remains elevated as Trump's tariffs take hold
rows.standfirst: Inflation remained elevated last month as President Trump's tariffs continued to make their way into the prices that consumers pay. The average cost of living in July was up 2.7%.

rows.title: U.S. and China extend tariff truce deadline for another 3 months
rows.standfirst: President Trump's executive order extends a reprieve from the threat of rising tariffs between the world's two largest economies.

rows.title: An Israeli airstrike kills a prominent Al Jazeera journalist and colleagues in Gaza
rows.standfirst: Al Jazeera's Anas al-Sharif and five of his colleagues at the network were killed in an Israeli airstrike targeting Gaza's most recognized television journalist.

rows.title: The arduous system for getting aid into Gaza
rows.standfirst: Insulin needles. Sleeping bags. Nutella. These are items Arwa Damon’s charity — International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance — has tried to send to Gaza and Israel has rejected. It’s a glimpse into the harsh reality of a humanitarian crisis with no end in sight. Today on the show, we talk to Damon about the economics of running a humanitarian nonprofit and what’s stopping more aid from reaching Gaza.

rows.title: Ford says it will roll out a cheaper electric pickup truck
rows.standfirst: Ford announced it will retool its Louisville Assembly Plant to focus on electric trucks. Its goal: to bring down prices for U.S. buyers and compete with Chinese EV makers on the global market.

rows.title: Trump says Nvidia will hand the U.S. 15% of its H20 chip sales to China
rows.standfirst: The president said that Nvidia would pay the government in exchange for easing export restrictions — and that he'd initially asked for a larger cut.

rows.title: Trump's tariff revenue has skyrocketed. But how big is it, really?
rows.standfirst: President Trump's new tariffs are pouring in. But it's still only a fraction of overall government revenues — and falls short of new spending in the recent Republican megabill.

rows.title: Factories from GE to Kraft Heinz lose immigrant workers, stressing those who remain
rows.standfirst: Trump campaigned on helping American workers through his immigration policies. Now that he's revoked work authorization for thousands of immigrants, those left behind are feeling taxed by their absence.

rows.title: With Fed under pressure, Jerome Powell prepares for a high-stakes speech
rows.standfirst: The Fed chair will speak Friday at an annual economic symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyo. The speech comes as the central bank is under mounting pressure from the White House to lower interest rates.

rows.title: Walmart says tariff costs are rising 'each week' and will continue
rows.standfirst: The world's largest retailer — like many others — has been absorbing most of the increased costs, but raising prices of some goods.

rows.title: Far fewer Canadians are visiting the U.S. this year, new numbers show
rows.standfirst: Canadian residents made just 1.7 million return trips by motor vehicle back into their country from the U.S. in July, a nearly 37% decline over the same month in 2024, according to Statistics Canada.

rows.title: What happens when railroads get hitched
rows.standfirst: Two freight-rail giants could make history if their $85 billion merger gets approved. Union Pacific’s proposed marriage with Norfolk Southern would create the first coast-to-coast rail network. So why hasn’t it happened before now? Today on the show, the business of train mergers.

rows.title: Trump calls for resignation of Fed governor in latest line of attack
rows.standfirst: President Trump is calling for the resignation of Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook after a Trump ally accused her of making false statements on mortgage applications.

rows.title: Cobalt-free batteries reign in Chinese EVs. Why not the US?
rows.standfirst: There’s been an era-defining race underway between two types of batteries used in electric vehicles: lithium batteries that use cobalt, and ones that use iron phosphate. Cobalt, a metal with a checkered human rights record, has been in the lead. Until recently.

rows.title: Govt 7: Trade blocks and blockages (Trade Policy)
rows.standfirst: Find all episodes of Planet Money Summer School here.

rows.title: Summer School 7: Trade blocks and blockages
rows.standfirst: Tariffs are the favorite tool of our current president, but there are lots of other ways that governments insert themselves into the free exchange of goods and services. Some of these trade barriers are so insidious and have been going on for so long that it may surprise you that they even exist.

rows.title: Walmart recalls frozen shrimp over potential radioactive contamination
rows.standfirst: The risk from the recalled shrimp is "quite low," said Donald Schaffner, a food safety expert at Rutgers University. Cesium-137 is a byproduct of nuclear reactions.

rows.title: Home Depot keeps quiet on immigration raids outside its doors
rows.standfirst: The home-improvement chain is now one of the companies most caught up in Trump's immigration crackdown. The retailer's history with day laborers is long. So far, it's choosing to keep its distance.

rows.title: Air Canada flights slowly resume after flight attendants agree to end their strike
rows.standfirst: The flight attendants' union said a new agreement guarantees members will be paid for work performed while planes are on the ground, resolving one of the major issues that drove the strike.

rows.title: Businesses face 'chaos' as EPA aims to repeal its authority over climate pollution
rows.standfirst: A lot of companies want the EPA in charge of setting national climate regulations because it helps shield them from lawsuits and creates a predictable environment in which to make investments.

rows.title: How algorithms are changing the way we speak
rows.standfirst: Social media has birthed an entire lexicon replicated by millions online — even if these words don’t actually mean skibidi. On today’s show, we talk to author Adam Aleksic about how TikTok and Instagram's engagement metrics, and viral memes, are rewiring our brains and transforming language at warp speed.

rows.title: 'SNL' castmember Bowen Yang shares a piece of 'cultural contraband' from his youth
rows.standfirst: Growing up with immigrant parents, first in Canada and then in the U.S., Yang was "obsessed" with pop culture and Saturday Night Live . Now he's up for an Emmy for his performances on the venerated sketch series.

rows.title: Newsmax pays $67 million to settle defamation case linked to 2020 election coverage
rows.standfirst: The right-wing news channel Newsmax has agreed to pay $67 million to Dominion Voting Systems over its coverage of the 2020 presidential election. A trial had been scheduled for October.

rows.title: Spirit Airlines files for bankruptcy for 2nd time in less than a year
rows.standfirst: The budget carrier filed for fresh bankruptcy protection months after emerging from a Chapter 11 reorganization. The airline said it plans to keep flying as usual during the restructuring process.

rows.title: Dear Life Kit: Do I have to buy birthday gifts for my 18 nieces and nephews?
rows.standfirst: Experts answer a round of finance questions from NPR's audience, including how to financially support a friend with Stage 4 cancer and how to stop paying for your parents.

rows.title: AI and Nvidia have been bright spots in an uncertain economy, but there are doubts now
rows.standfirst: This past week, AI darling Nvidia reported blockbuster financial results that beat analysts' expectations. But investors weren't impressed and the stock price dropped.

rows.title: Lisa Cook and the fight for the Fed
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve has been under intense pressure from President Donald Trump as he pushes for more control over the historically independent agency. The Fed is tasked with keeping inflation and unemployment under control, and it’s supposed to be insulated from politics so it can do whatever is necessary for the economy. But Trump has been openly saying he wants interest rates to be lower. A lot lower.

rows.title: Most of President Trump's tariffs are illegal, U.S. court rules
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, in Washington, D.C., delayed enforcing its decision, which is expected to be appealed to the Supreme Court.

rows.title: AI creeps in, KATSEYE milkshakes, and China says “Zaijian!” to US soybeans
rows.standfirst: It’s … Indicators of the Week! Our weekly look at some of the most fascinating economic numbers from the news. On today’s episode: AI shuts out youth from the grind, China leaves U.S. soybeans behind, Gap has the then-and-now in marketing mind. Related episodes:

rows.title: Federal judge says Kari Lake can't fire Voice of America director
rows.standfirst: A federal judge has ruled that Trump administration official Kari Lake can't unilaterally fire the director of Voice of America.

rows.title: With no federal facial recognition law, states rush to fill void
rows.standfirst: Nearly two dozen states have passed laws regulating how tech companies collect data from our faces, eyes and voices. It comes as Congress has yet to pass any facial recognition technology.

rows.title: Fed governor Lisa Cook sues Trump over firing
rows.standfirst: Lisa Cook is challenging the president's attempt to remove her from office based on what she says is "an unsubstantiated allegation" of mortgage fraud prior to her Senate confirmation as governor.

rows.title: This rule made many online purchases dirt cheap for U.S. consumers. Now it's ending
rows.standfirst: On Friday, the U.S. is ending its de minimis rule that made it easy for cheap goods to reach consumers. The change will affect roughly 4 million such packages processed each day.

rows.title: 'AI slop' videos may be annoying, but they're racking up views — and ad money
rows.standfirst: Critics say that "slop" videos made with generative AI are often repetitive or useless. But they get millions of views — and platforms are grappling with what to do about them.

rows.title: What olive oil tells us about Trump's tariffs
rows.standfirst: Trump's tariffs are making business harder for international olive oil producers and it turns out those tariffs are even complicating other parts of the Trump administration's agenda, too.

rows.title: Should the government be in the business of business?
rows.standfirst: What happens when the federal government owns part of a company? That’s one of MANY questions about federal policy right now, as the Trump Administration aggressively pushes for stakes — and oversight — of major private companies.

rows.title: Brands are loving Taylor Swift's engagement. Do they need to calm down?
rows.standfirst: Companies from Pillsbury to Invisalign to Olipop are cheering — and trying to cash in on — the couple's engagement. Experts spoke to NPR about how brands can strike a better balance.

rows.title: Take The Planet Money Summer School Quiz In Political Economy
rows.standfirst: Think you have what it takes to successfully manipulate the market and build a domestic industry from the ground up? If so, these eight questions stand between you and your Summer School diploma in political cconomy.
